Hi Naomi / Irene,

We've started bundling the artifacts for the SOC 2 submission and uploaded an initial manifest to Vendr. Quick questions before we run the bulk presign:

- Does Redwood accept presigned S3 uploads for CAIQ/SIG artifacts, or do you prefer us to push directly to the vendor portal (OneTrust/Vendr)?
- For log files (S3 access logs, CloudTrail extracts), do you require SHA256 hashes and an explicit "chain-of-custody" signature (name/email + timestamp) in the manifest?
- What is Redwood's retention expectation for raw evidence? Our legal team prefers 7 years for auditability, but SOC 2 evidence is commonly kept 2-3 years; will that affect acceptance?

I've attached an evidence_manifest.csv (sample rows) and a screenshot of the portal ACLs (screenshot_acl.png). We can open a presign window starting Wed if that helps.

Thanks,

Hi Emily — thanks for the manifest and ACL screenshot. Short answers up front: we accept presigned S3 uploads to a temporary bucket we provide (preferred for large bulk), and we require SHA256 hashes for binary artifacts. A few clarifying asks so our ingestion team can sign off: 

1) Can you add a "submitted_by" column to the manifest with full name + email + ISO timestamp for each artifact? That will satisfy our chain-of-custody fielding.
2) For logs: include a separate CSV row per file with the SHA256 and the UTC timestamp of the extract.
3) Retention: Redwood doesn't prevent you from keeping evidence for 7 years, but our retention index for audit artifacts is configurable per-account. Default acceptance is a 3-year retention policy; if you need longer we can set a 7-year retention flag on your account, but that requires a short MSA amendment for archived retention (I can route to finance/GC if needed).

Operationally, next steps:
- If you confirm presign uploads, we'll create a dedicated presign bucket and post a short presign schedule (24h windows, one-time use links).
- Please update the manifest and re-upload.
- Irene, can you confirm the SHA/hash and KMS expectations below?

Here's the quick playbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/portal-delegation-playbook — the presign guidelines are on page 4 (upload TTL, one-use links, and required manifest fields).

Happy to jump on a quick call Wednesday morning if that's easier.

—Naomi

Hi all,

Quick technical confirmation from Redwood Security:

- Presigned uploads: accepted. We will provide a short-lived presign bucket and require one-time-use presigned PUTs.
- Hashing: SHA256 is required for any binary evidence (logs, binaries, signed PDFs). We'll store the hash in the ingestion metadata and verify on receipt.
- Chain-of-custody: the manifest must include a "submitted_by" field with name, email, and ISO-8601 timestamp. That field is surfaced in our SOC 2 evidence index for auditors.
- KMS & signing: if you want the evidence envelope to carry a Redwood-managed HMAC signature we can do that; otherwise we accept your provided SHA256 and a signed POAM or cover letter. If you do want HMAC, provide the KMS key identifier in the manifest (format: arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/KEYID) and we will handshake for a short-lived signing token.
- Retention: default account-level retention is 3 years. If FinBank requires 7-year retention we will enable an extended-retention flag; that will surface a small archive fee and needs the legal amendment Naomi mentioned.

Other operational notes:
- Preferred presign TTL: 24 hours. Links must be one-time-use (we verify ETag + hash on ingest).
- Redaction: if any artifacts contain PII, please apply the redaction guidance in the attached POI redaction doc before upload; we will reject evidence containing unredacted personal data when not scoped.

Attachments:
- poi-redaction-guidance.pdf

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
